meta.title: Shared dependency failure across unrelated flows (transco-cache)
meta.faultOneLine: hip-fwk-transco-cache pod restart; Connection refused errors on 32 half-flows in 4 projects

diagnosis.incident_summary: From 00:55 UTC, unrelated EMEA flows (sales orders, invoices, price lists, returns across four projects) failed with the same 'Connection refused' to the shared hip-fwk-transco-cache; that pod's memory had climbed to 93% and it was killed and restarted at 00:20, and it was Ready again at 01:13:41.

hypotheses.cause: The shared hip-fwk-transco-cache pod ran out of memory, was killed and restarted, and was not serving on port 8080 for a period, so every half-flow that calls it failed with 'Connection refused' until it was Ready again.

supports.why: Cache pod memory reaches 93%, 43.9 points above its baseline, two minutes before it restarts.
The pod restarts at 00:20 with exit code 137 (killed), the first event on the shared dependency.
The first failure names exactly this service and port: Connection refused to hip-fwk-transco-cache...:8080.
46 exchanges fail in five minutes with the identical reason, and the count spreads across 23 half-flows in 4 projects; by 01:15 it is 148 across 32 half-flows (e-0323).
All 41 other pods in the namespace are Ready, node network errors are 0 and no other service reports ConnectionRefused: the fault is local to the cache.
The pod is Ready again at 01:13:41, which matches the end of the failures and the successful replays (e-0351).

contradicts.why: Transcoding calls run normally at 00:45 (4,351 per 5 minutes vs 4,300 baseline), 25 minutes after the restart: the restart alone does not explain failures starting at 00:55.
By 01:14 the pod shows Running and Ready with restartCount=1, so an inspection then finds nothing obviously broken.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: The pod's readiness history for 00:20 to 01:14. A NotReady window covering the failures would raise this to High; continuous Ready status with no events would move weight to a network or discovery cause.

hypotheses.cause: A transient network, DNS or service-endpoint disruption inside the cluster between the callers and the cache service.

supports.why: Replays succeed minutes later without any change, which is how a transient network fault would look.
The cache pod itself is healthy when inspected, so the target looks fine from the outside.

contradicts.why: CoreDNS p99 is 4 ms, node network errors are 0, and none of the 41 other pods reports ConnectionRefused: a cluster network fault would not spare every other service.
The error text names the cache service specifically rather than a name-resolution or timeout failure.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: Service endpoint history showing the cache service had endpoints throughout the window, plus failures from callers of other services in the same period, would raise this.

hypotheses.cause: A load spike overwhelmed the cache and made it refuse connections.

supports.why: Memory climbs to 93% before the restart, consistent with the cache being under heavy use.

contradicts.why: Transcoding call volume at 00:15 is 4,339 per 5 minutes against a 4,300 baseline: no spike.
Volume is still normal at 00:45 (4,351), just before the failures begin.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: Per-caller request rates for the cache showing a burst before 00:20 would raise this.

ruled_out.candidate: Faults in each failing source or target system
ruled_out.reason: Alerts arrive from four unrelated projects (e.g. e-0048 Amazon returns, e-0052 Kepler price list, e-0057 SAPIT invoices) with the same error text naming the same dependency, so no single source or target explains them.
Lag rises only on the four groups whose flows call the cache and is 0 on the other three (e-0235). It is a consequence of the failures, and it falls again as replays complete (e-0413).

ruled_out.candidate: Change records in the window (CHG4400600 to CHG4400605)
ruled_out.reason: None touches the cache or its namespace: a TLS renewal on one Kepler ingress (e-0034), a Schema Registry key rotation (e-0024), a Manhattan report time change (e-0020), a sandbox Workato recipe (e-0536), a dev MFT purge (e-0540) and a mapping fix on a FOM flow (e-0322). One Kepler certificate cannot explain failures in SAPIT and Amazon flows.

ruled_out.candidate: The 'Plant field missing' mapping errors on inventory flows
ruled_out.reason: Different projects and error text (e-0454, e-0455) with no shared dependency with the cache; they are a separate matter and no recovery is proposed for them.

ruled_out.candidate: Standing host alerts: SGLORHIPQETLPC1 swap 90% and FRHIPGQAMFTSI01 CPU 98%
ruled_out.reason: Recurring non-production host alerts (e-0009, e-0018) present before the incident and unrelated to the cache pod.

checks.action: Get the cache pod's restart history and readiness timeline for 00:15 to 01:15
checks.command: kubectl describe pod hip-fwk-transco-cache-644827de5-fmmh9 -n hip-cloud-esb; kubectl get events -n hip-cloud-esb --field-selector involvedObject.name=hip-fwk-transco-cache-644827de5-fmmh9
checks.if_result_a: OOMKilled at 00:19-00:20 and a NotReady window covering the failures: supports hypothesis 1
checks.if_result_b: Continuously Ready with no events in the window: supports a network or discovery cause (hypothesis 2)

checks.action: Group the 'Connection refused' failures by project to confirm one shared dependency
checks.command: Sonar: filter event.reason:"Connection refused*transco-cache*" and chart count by project, 00:50 to 01:15
checks.if_result_a: Many unrelated projects fail together: a shared dependency (hypothesis 1)
checks.if_result_b: One project only: a local fault in that flow, not the cache

checks.action: Check the cache pod's memory limit against its usage
checks.command: kubectl top pod hip-fwk-transco-cache-644827de5-fmmh9 -n hip-cloud-esb; kubectl get pod -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}'
checks.if_result_a: Usage close to the limit before the restart: memory sizing is the underlying fault (hypotheses 1 and 3)
checks.if_result_b: Ample headroom: look for a leak or a burst instead

checks.action: Confirm the cache service had endpoints throughout the window
checks.command: kubectl get endpoints hip-fwk-transco-cache -n hip-cloud-esb -o yaml, and the endpoint controller events for 00:50 to 01:15
checks.if_result_a: Endpoints empty during the window: supports hypothesis 1

business_flows: PROCESSOUT flows; 32 half-flows in 4 projects in total
downstream_degraded: Kafka lag on sapit-01-default, kepler-01-default, procout-01-default, amazon-01-default (e-0235)
blast_radius.business_objects_at_risk: 148 FAILED exchanges (cumulative to 01:15, e-0323): sales orders, invoices, price lists and return notifications; replays have already succeeded for some (e-0351).

recovery.proposal: Replay the failed exchanges in a single approved batch now that the cache is Ready (01:13:41) and the failure reason has stopped, then check the four affected consumer groups drain. Afterwards raise the cache pod's memory limit or add a memory alert so a repeat is visible before the kill.
recovery.risk: A replay can deliver duplicates downstream for exchanges that partly completed (invoices and sales orders are the concern); replayed exchanges may end as WARNING 'as per design'. Raising the memory limit needs a rollout of the cache deployment.
recovery.rollback: Replay is additive and needs no rollback; if duplicates appear, stop the batch and reconcile from the source systems. A memory-limit change is rolled back by reverting the deployment to its previous revision.

diagnosis.post_incident_note: #01 -Analysis/Root cause: [Hypothesis, pending pod readiness history] hip-fwk-transco-cache memory reached 93% at 00:18 and the pod restarted with exit code 137 at 00:20; from 00:55 every half-flow calling it failed with 'Connection refused ...:8080' (148 failed exchanges across 32 half-flows in 4 unrelated projects by 01:15); the pod was Ready again at 01:13:41 and replays then succeeded; the other 41 pods in hip-cloud-esb showed no network errors. #02-Resolution/Flow state: [Proposed, awaiting approval] replay the failed exchanges in one batch; review the cache memory limit. #03-Doc used: KB0041802 (replay failed exchange). #04- Related records (PRB, Change, Incident, RITM...): INC10790505 with its duplicates; no related change record found (CHG4400600 to CHG4400605 reviewed and excluded).

diff.changed_summary: The late Kubernetes batch shows the cache was OOMKilled at its 2Gi limit at 00:19:41 and its readiness probe failed from 00:52:07 to 01:13:41 while it rehydrated, which explains the 35-minute gap and matches the failure window exactly; the cache hypothesis moves from Moderate to High and the network hypothesis is effectively closed.

rank_before.cause: Transient cluster network or DNS disruption

rank_after.cause: Transient cluster network or DNS disruption

what_changed: e-late-0001 answers the check ordered first: the pod was OOMKilled at 00:19:41 (limit 2Gi, exit 137) and its readiness probe failed from 00:52:07 until 01:13:41.
That closes the gap named in hypothesis 1's contradicts column: the pod restarted at 00:20 but was still rehydrating and not Ready when the failures began at 00:55.
The same record states no other pod in hip-cloud-esb reported network errors, which removes the remaining support for a cluster network cause.
Recovery is unchanged in action but better justified: the failure window is fully bounded, so the batch replay covers exactly the exchanges that failed between 00:52 and 01:14.

diagnosisAfterOverrides.incident_summary: From 00:55 UTC unrelated EMEA flows failed with 'Connection refused' to the shared hip-fwk-transco-cache, which was OOMKilled at its 2Gi limit at 00:19:41 and was not Ready from 00:52:07 until 01:13:41 while it rehydrated.

1.what_would_change_this: Only evidence that the pod was Ready and serving throughout 00:52 to 01:14 would lower it now.

2.what_would_change_this: Effectively closed: the readiness failure window and the absence of network errors elsewhere explain the failures without a network cause.
